key_insight: The paper proposes a smooth, explicit elastoplastic-damage material update that avoids local Newton solves by using closed-form active/frozen branches driven by a history variable.
engineering_relevance: This gives graphics simulation a compact, vectorizable constitutive update that preserves irreversibility and residual deformation while staying simple to implement in explicit solvers.
method: Softplus generates a candidate equivalent plastic strain for smooth activation.
A max-history projection enforces irreversibility, while a deviatoric plastic-strain tensor stores residual direction.
An exponential damage variable is updated analytically from one response energy, with no local Newton iteration.
evidence_signal: Across cyclic tension, cantilever bending, platen compression, and a torus test, the method reproduced residual deformation and monotone internal variables, while the baseline J2 return mapping was 1.51–3.08× faster as a kernel.
watch_item: The approach is intended for isotropic proportional or near-proportional loading; accuracy drops sharply for large loading-direction changes and it is not a general replacement for return mapping.
paper_title: A Smooth Explicit Elastoplastic--Damage Update for Graphics Simulation
